cases.name: Civic hub between bar and commons
cases.organizing_principle: A single academic bar holds all classrooms, with art and music on its ground floor. A compact civic hub of administration, medical and custodial, topped by media, sits between the bar and a double-height commons.
cases.main_tradeoff: All movement between classrooms and commons passes through the civic hub. This centralizes supervision but lengthens daily lunch and gym routes. The hub and commons give up the three-floor preference.
unresolved_notes: The hub's upper floor holds only media, so its floor plates are uneven. Stack balance needs a dimensional check.
Media is on the hub's top floor (floor 2) above administration. This meets the preference only if a two-floor hub is acceptable.
Kitchen receiving depends on custodial in the hub. The service adjacency across the link needs checking.
The single-level commons footprint is likely near the length and ratio envelope.

cases.name: Civic-academic stack with ground enrichment wing
cases.organizing_principle: Core academic stacks over a ground-floor civic front, with media on the bar's top floor. Special education and art and music share an accessible one-story wing. The commons is the third mass, and all three masses are linked to each other.
cases.main_tradeoff: Special education gets ground-level access and sits next to the arts, but is separated from general classrooms, which weakens inclusion. Two single-story masses give up the three-floor preference.
unresolved_notes: The single-story wing must meet the 80-ft special-education width as well as the length and ratio limits. Needs checking.
Custodial receiving is in the academic mass, away from the kitchen. The service route through the link needs checking.
Without site geometry, it is unknown whether all three direct links can be built.

cases.name: Commons with arts loft
cases.organizing_principle: Gym and dining fill a double-height ground volume, with art and music raised onto a top-floor loft overlooking it. The classroom bar keeps special education at grade. A civic mass puts media above administration.
cases.main_tradeoff: Raising the arts over the commons gives that mass a third level and links music to the stage. It gives up the ground-floor arts preference and adds long-span structure and acoustic separation demands.
unresolved_notes: Art and music above the double-height void leaves floor 2 of the commons unoccupied. Structural and acoustic feasibility are untested.
The civic block is two floors. Media's top-floor position holds only if the stack balances.
There is no direct link between commons and civic block, so the after-hours visitor route is unresolved.

cases.name: Detached campus pavilions
cases.organizing_principle: One consolidated learning house holds administration, medical, special education, classrooms and media. The commons and an arts-and-service pavilion stand apart. They are linked to each other and reached from the house across open ground.
cases.main_tradeoff: Detaching the commons and arts makes after-hours use and phasing simpler. Students must cross open ground every day for lunch, gym and arts, which weakens supervision, weather protection and single-entry control.
unresolved_notes: Daily outdoor crossings may conflict with admin-controlled secure entry. The brief does not address this.
All of special education plus admin and medical on the ground floor may exceed one floor plate of the bar. Stack balance needs checking.
Two single-story pavilions give up the three-floor preference.

cases.name: Support bar with academic spine
cases.organizing_principle: Special education is paired with administration, medical and media in a two-story support bar, keeping specialized services together. Core academic shares its bar with ground-floor arts and custodial, and that bar links to both other masses.
cases.main_tradeoff: Clustering special education with administrative and medical support helps services and supervision. It distances those students from grade-level peers, and the two-story support bar may be too small for its required width.
unresolved_notes: The support bar's area may fall short of the minimum length implied by the 80-ft width and ratio limits. Needs checking.
Media is on floor 2, the support bar's top floor, so the preference is met only in a two-floor mass.
There is no direct link from administration to the commons, so event visitors route through the academic bar.

collection_differences: Cases differ in where art and music sit (academic bar ground floor, enrichment wing, commons loft, detached pavilion). They also differ in whether special education joins the classroom bar or a separate wing or support bar, and which mass holds administration and media (civic mass, academic bar top, or support bar). Connection layouts range from a civic hub (S01) and full triangle (S02) to an academic spine (S03, S05) and a detached campus (S04). Only S03 places program over the commons void. All keep gym and dining together in one ground-level double-height mass with admin at grade. Several give up the three-floor or ground-floor arts preferences.
